name: Hyperreal CGI mechanism / 'x-ray' shot (inside the material) + villain monologue

shots.visual: Extreme macro CGI: the camera dives into a chain link until the metal layers are visible like geological strata
shots.audio_text: Villain VO (gravelly): "I'm Tarnish. I live on cheap jewellery."

shots.visual: Cutaway: a cheap plated chain under shower water; the thin top layer flakes off, grey metal shows through
shots.audio_text: "A little water. A little sweat. I eat the plating right off."

shots.visual: Same water hits the PVD chain; droplets bead and roll off; a glowing bonded layer stays intact
shots.audio_text: Villain, confused: "Wait... why can't I get in?"

shots.visual: Labelled cross-section: stainless steel core / bonded PVD gold layer
shots.audio_text: Narrator (warm): "14K PVD gold, bonded to stainless steel. Nothing to flake."

shots.visual: Real product footage: a hand in the sea wearing the stack
shots.audio_text: Villain, defeated: "Fine. I'll go find a $9 necklace."

qa_checklist: Hook lands in the first 1.5 s (video) or is readable at thumbnail size (static / slide 1).
Removal test: delete the product from the script. If it still makes sense, rewrite so the product is the payoff.
Matches the reference structure (same beat order and length band) before any creative twist.
Uses only real product imagery for the product; AI is for backgrounds, characters or b-roll, and is disclosed where required.
Every claim is on the brand's approved-claims list (PDP); no invented stats, reviews, doctors or customers.
Captions burned in and inside the safe zone; sound-off still understandable.
One clear CTA that matches the landing page offer.
Three hook variants delivered for the same body (test hooks, not whole new ads).
Avoid: The CGI must match the real material and process; don't show layers or effects that don't exist.
Avoid: Show the cheap plating failing in a way that is true; don't exaggerate it.
Avoid: Finish on real product footage; ads that are all CGI read as fake.
Avoid: Keep the villain under 4 lines; it is a device, not the star.
inputs: BRAND (name, product, price, offer, audience, proof points, banned claims)
